children.description_long: On February 3, 2025, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum announced that he had signed six Secretary’s Orders on his first day in office. The Department described Secretary’s Order 3418, “Unleashing American Energy,” as aligning Interior with the president’s energy policy, encouraging energy exploration and production on federal lands and waters, and requiring review of agency actions that could burden domestic energy-resource development. The order also directed review of certain appropriations. This card records the policy direction and review instructions, not a measured change in drilling, leasing outcomes, or environmental conditions. The original entry’s Wyoming acreage and migration-corridor claims concern later lease events and are separated into another child. No 28-day permitting guarantee, acreage figure, or migration-corridor effect is carried into this copy because the accessed evidence for the February order does not establish those claims. title: DHS Ends CSRB Memberships; Easterly's Departure Is a Separate Claim
description_short: DHS Ends CSRB Memberships; Easterly's Departure Is a Separate Claim
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, DHS Acting Secretary Benjamine Huffman terminated current advisory-committee memberships, including the Cyber Safety Review Board, while it was investigating Salt Typhoon. description_long: This internal reconstruction separates two claims that the frozen entry joined. SANS and TechTarget report that a January 20 memo from Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman terminated advisory committee memberships, including the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB), while it was examining the Salt Typhoon telecom intrusion. Those sources support a discrete DHS advisory-board action. The supplied packet separately says CISA Director Jen Easterly's tenure ended at the presidential transition. It supplies no direct source for her departure date or mechanism; the CISA leadership page retrieved in this session is a current directory and does not establish a January 2025 dismissal. Nothing accessed shows that Trump dismissed Easterly through the DHS memo, that her departure halted the CSRB inquiry, or that all federal cyber defense work stopped. The two issues therefore need separate records. This draft keeps the DHS action as a sourced child and treats the CISA departure as unverified supplied input. The frozen entry's claims about an unfinished report, critical-infrastructure exposure, and broad expert condemnation are not reproduced as established results. Keep the compound item internal until the separate departure claim is sourced.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: An internal memo issued January 20, 2025, from Acting Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Benjamine Huffman, terminated all advisory committee positions. Among those dismissed were the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB), a committee responsible for “study[ing] major cyber incidents and recommend[ing] improvements,” comprising private sector experts and government cybersecurity officials. title: Internal Draft: Supplied April 2025 Pell-Restriction Claim Remains Unverified

description_medium: The supplied record alleges that an April 2025 rule removed Pell access for several groups, but no contemporaneous rule or source is included. description_long: This internal draft records the supplied allegation that, in April 2025, the administration restricted Pell eligibility for undocumented students, short-term credential learners, and students at institutions cited under new anti-DEI rules. The packet contains no April rule text, contemporaneous notice, or source linking those groups to one action, so the allegation remains unverified. The accessible Education Department release is dated July 2025: it describes an interpretive rule affecting eligibility verification for certain career, technical, and adult-education benefits, and says Pell Grants and federal student loans remained unavailable to people who did not qualify under existing rules. The Department said its interpretive rule was not binding; the accessed page also records a later court-related stay of potential enforcement through September 10, 2025. A separate Workforce Pell announcement says qualifying short-term programs could receive Pell funding beginning July 1, 2026, which does not support an April 2025 elimination of short-term Pell. The supplied claims about anti-DEI institution exclusions, reduced award amounts, and projected impacts on students are not established by these pages and are not presented as findings. The April date, covered populations, legal mechanism, and consequences remain unknown. Keep this draft internal until an April rule or reliable contemporaneous reporting is available.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: As part of a lawsuit, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) has agreed to stay potential enforcement through September 10, 2025 of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Act, as amended, (PRWORA), to the degree that such enforcement actions are consistent with ED’s interpretive rule regarding PRWORA as announced in the “Clarification of Federal Public Benefits Under the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act” 90 Fed. Reg. 30,896 (July 11, 2025).

insight_facts: The July 2025 Education Department release says Pell grants and federal student loans remained inaccessible to people who did not meet existing eligibility requirements.
The later Workforce Pell program allowed qualifying short-term programs to receive Pell beginning July 1, 2026.

evidence_map.fact: Existing Pell eligibility rule described by ED; does not support a new April 2025 cutoff.
evidence_map.quote: continue to be inaccessible to illegal immigrants.
evidence_map.source_excerpt: In an interpretive rule issued today, the Department rescinded a Dear Colleague letter from the Clinton Administration that enabled non-qualified illegal aliens to access federal public benefits in contravention of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA). The interpretive rule also ensures that postsecondary education programs authorized under the Higher Education Act (HEA), such as Pell Grants and student loans, continue to be inaccessible to illegal immigrants.

evidence_map.quote: Beginning on July 1, 2026, students will be able to receive Pell Grants for enrollment in high-quality, short-term educational programs
evidence_map.source_excerpt: Beginning on July 1, 2026, students will be able to receive Pell Grants for enrollment in high-quality, short-term educational programs that prepare them for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand jobs.

uncertainties: No accessed source establishes an April 2025 rule matching the supplied combined claim or confirms its date, legal text, groups, or effective date.

The claimed projected enrollment and completion impacts are unsupported; no quantities or causal outcomes are asserted.
The Workforce Pell page text was accessed, but its publication timestamp conflicts with the date in supplied evidence; treat the announcement date as unresolved.
